sentences.text:
1. Accused No.1 in Crime No.162/2023 registered by Harapanahalli Police Station, Vijayanagara District for the offence punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code is before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. FIR in Crime No.162/2023 was registered by Harapanahalli Police Station, Vijayanagara District,
against Kumara and another for the above said offence.

Apprehending arrest in the said case, the petitioner who is arraigned as accused no.1 in the remand application of accused Nos.2 to 4 who were arrested during the course of investigation had filed Crl.Misc.P.No.5874/2023 before the Court of III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Ballari (sitting at Hosapete), which was dismissed on 22.12.2023.

entities.text: Court of III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that NC: 2024:KHC-D:863 accused Nos.2 to 4 have been granted regular bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. and the petitioner has no criminal antecedents.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the bail application.
She submits that substantial amount is required to be recovered from the petitioner and therefore, his custodial interrogation is necessary.
Accordingly, she prays to dismiss the petition.

6. In the complaint dated 06.08.2023 lodged by Lakkappa Holkar, it is mentioned that accused Nos.1 and 2 had contacted him over phone and had informed him that while demolishing their old house, they had found a mud pot which contained gold coins and since they were in necessity of money, they intended to sell the gold coins at lower rate.
The complainant allegedly had given sum of Rs.12,00,000/- to the accused persons and accused had handed over 3 bags allegedly containing 1 kg. of gold coins.
The gold coins handed over by the accused persons was found to be fake.
Accused Nos.2 to 4 were arrested NC: 2024:KHC-D:863 during the course of investigation.
From the custody of arrested accused substantial amount of money has been recovered by the police.
Accused No.4 is said to be the brother of accused no.1 and he has stated that a sum of Rs.2,25,000/- was kept for himself by accused no.1.

2 7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From perusal of material available on record, it is seen that the petitioner is the master mind and accused nos.2 to 4 had acted as per his instructions.
As rightly contended by the learned HCGP substantial amount which is taken by the petitioner towards his share is yet to be recovered by the prosecution.
8. Under these circumstances, I am of the opinion that, it is not a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
